body.text:
Not to replace current tags but to introduce extra layer on top of it with `/releases` and `/releases/{id}` pages.

# Reason

git annotated tag has 3 problems. 2 limitations and 1 issue.

- We can't support rich text there because it is semantically plaintext and **NOT** markdown.\
  Well, we can probably introduce something like `Markup-Format: commonmark` trailer, but that will still lack features like image upload or user/ticket mentions (due to how [TFM works](https://tangled.org/tangled.org/core/issues/762).) To support full TFM spec, we need `org.tangled.markup.markdown` object.
- We can't support extra metadata
  > what metadata?
  - basic flags like:
    - prerelease
    - make_latest
    - hide_artifact_links
  - link to milestones
  - audit informations like gitlab's evidences
- Attachments are loosely linked.\
  Because `org.tangled.repo.artifact` currently use object-id but not all tags have their own object-id (only annotated tags do,) Artifacts are not directly linked to the target tag. Both point to specific commit-id and we match on that. But, lightweight tags can *technically* move to different commit.

# Spec

### record-key

any format.

Same name from git tag is preferred but usually normalized. So tags like `sdk/trace/v1.31.0` will have sidecar release record `sdk-trace-v1.31.0`. Note that this is *not* how release objects will point to a tag.

### Record example:

```json
{
  "$type": "org.tangled.track.release",
  "subject": {
    "$type": "#tag",
    "tag": "sdk/trace/v1.31.0"
  },
  "title": {
    "$type": "org.tangled.markup.markdown#inline",
    "text": "sdk/trace: `v1.31.0`"
  },
  "body": {
    "$type": "org.tangled.markup.markdown",
    "text": "..."
  },
  "attachments": [
    { "$type": "#attachment", "filename": "...", "blob": { } },
    { "$type": "#attachment", "filename": "...", "blob": { } }
  ],
  "createdAt": "..."
}
```

- release can have rich title and body, similar to tickets.
- attachments are inlined so tagger can sign whole record including the uploaded attachments.

# Open questions

### Should we mix releases and tags in one list like GitHub does?

#### Pros
- They serve same role and few devs might not even use releases, so merging everything into "tag" is good.
- "latest" works like imaginary tag
#### Cons
- Tags and releases are not same. It's wrong to serve release content when path literally says `/tags/*`. Even if we use it like sidecar record (similar to what we are doing with `org.tangled.repo.artifact` today,) those are not really part of tag while rendered as if they are. This will introduce same problem from GitHub.
- "latest" works like imaginary tag while it's not.

Currently API call limits to 100, but we can lazy-load more. Problem is interactive commit range selector UI. Pretty sure it won't work when there are a lot of commits. Even 50+ will be hard to manage.

Should we just drop the commit-range selector concept..? :thinking:
